folder_html:
LIVE AIR QUALITY

Near-surface fine-particulate (PM2.5) conditions from the CAMS atmospheric-composition analysis: a continuous field flagging wildfire-smoke intrusions, urban haze, and regional pollutant transport over the Great Lakes. Low values mark clean air; orange, red, and purple mark progressively degraded, unhealthy air. The underlying variable is PM2.5, identified as modeled output (CAMS analysis), not station observations.

Air-quality science (atmospheric chemistry and public-health exposure assessment) tracks PM2.5, particles under 2.5 micrometers that penetrate deep into lungs. Concentrations in micrograms per cubic meter map to health-based breakpoints (good, moderate, unhealthy for sensitive groups, unhealthy, very unhealthy). This layer shows modeled concentration, not aerosol optical depth, and is labeled as model output rather than station observations.


PM2.5 concentration in micrograms per cubic meter (CAMS model analysis, fixed EPA-anchored scale): LOWEST 0 green good → 12 moderate yellow → 35.4 unhealthy for sensitive groups orange → 55.4 unhealthy red → HIGHEST+ 150 purple very unhealthy (above clamps into purple). Same concentration always shows the same color. Modeled PM2.5 — not aerosol optical depth, not station observations.
